{{Short description|Greek-American mathematician (born 1941)}}
{{Distinguish|Mihalis Dafermos}}
[[File:Kroner, Dafermos, and LeVeque.jpg|thumb|Dafermos (center) at Oberwolfach in 2004. Photo courtesy [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|MFO]]]]
'''Constantine Michael Dafermos''' ([[Greek language|Greek]]: Κωνσταντίνος Δαφέρμος; born May 26, 1941, [[Athens]]) is a [[Greek-American]] [[applied mathematician]]. He received a diploma in civil
engineering from the [[National Technical University of Athens]] (1964) and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in mechanics from [[Johns Hopkins University]] under the direction of [[Jerald Ericksen]] (1967). He has been an assistant professor at [[Cornell University]] (1968–1971) and an associate professor (1971–1975) and professor (since 1975) in the Division of Applied Mathematics at [[Brown University]]. Since 1984, he has been the Alumni-Alumnae University Professor at Brown.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://research.brown.edu/pdf/1136831476.pdf?nocache=1255380913|title=CV|publisher=Constantine Dafermos|accessdate=2009-07-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719160730/http://research.brown.edu/pdf/1136831476.pdf?nocache=1255380913|archive-date=2011-07-19|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In recent years, his research has focused on nonlinear hyperbolic systems of [[Conservation law (physics)|conservation law]]s whose solutions spontaneously develop singularities propagating as [[shock waves]]. In particular, he is studying the interplay between [[thermodynamics]] and analysis in the theory of these systems and he is analyzing the fundamental role of [[entropy]] as a stabilizing agent.

In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref> 
In 2016 he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html|title=National Academy of Sciences Members and Foreign Associates Elected|department=News from the National Academy of Sciences|publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]]|date=May 3, 2016|accessdate=2016-05-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160506052951/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html|archive-date=May 6, 2016|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

==Awards==

*Honorary Doctorate, University of Athens, 1987.
*Honorary Doctorate, National Technical University (Greece), 1991.
*Honorary Doctorate, University of Crete, 2001.
*SIAM W.T. and Idalia Reid Prize, 2000.
*[[International Society for the Interaction of Mechanics and Mathematics|ISIMM prize]], 2014
*[[Norbert Wiener Prize in Applied Mathematics]], 2016 <ref>[https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=2892 Norbert Wiener Prize in Applied Mathematics 2016]</ref>

==Affiliations==

*Fellow American Academy of Arts and Sciences, 2001-.
*Correspondent Member, Academy of Athens, 1988-.
*Honorary Professor, Academia Sinica, China, 2004-.
*Member, Board of Governors, Weizmann Institute of Science (Israel), 1995-.
